content.title: About
content.content: Bologna is a cooked beef sausage traditionally made in Italy. It has a delicate pink color, soft texture, and a mildly sweet flavor with subtle spices. The product is commonly used in sandwiches, salads, and as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bologna gets its name from the city of Bologna, where it was first produced in the 19th century.
Traditional recipes use only beef, though modern versions may contain small amounts of pork or turkey.
The sausage is cooked at about 80 °C, making it ready to eat without further heating.
Bologna is often served cold, sliced thinly to highlight its tenderness.
In some countries Bologna is classified as a “soft sausage” rather than a “hot dog.”

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Beef in bologna provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from beef helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels and prevents anemia.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Bologna is rich in B12, B6, and niacin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb diets as it contributes minimal carbs.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Bologna can be high in salt, which is a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Some varieties contain nitrites and other preservatives that may be harmful in excess.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rare beef allergies can cause reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While not overly fatty, bologna’s calories should be considered in weight‑management plans.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bologna can be enjoyed as thin slices in sandwiches, added to salads, diced for appetizer platters, or used in hot dishes such as pasta.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store bologna in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. It typically remains fresh for 2–3 weeks after opening. When frozen, it retains quality for up to 2 months.
